title: Reroute slab circuit protector for intermittent latency waves across Hosted/Dedicated/Private
creator: Aisha Raman
description:
Summary: Multiple enterprise customers reported intermittent first-token latency spikes (TTFT) and reduced tokens/sec on a subset of requests routed to mixed-capacity slab pools. Spikes occur across Hosted, Dedicated and Private deployments, typically during short multi-tenant fanout bursts.

Observed behavior:
- TTFT spikes from baseline ~120ms to 800-1500ms for affected requests, sustained for 5–30s windows.
- Tokens/sec for affected requests falls 40–70% during windows.
- Spike correlates with partial KV-cache eviction activity and sudden kernel-selection churn on heterogeneous slabs.

Repro steps / telemetry used:
1) Replayed production traces (anonymized) against a staging cluster with the same slab mix and request mix.
2) Captured pprof of runtime during injected fanout bursts.
3) Instrumented per-slab kernel-select and KV eviction counters via telemetry.
4) Compared request traces across Hosted/Dedicated/Private to rule out network-induced noise.

Hypothesis: A race between the slab routing heuristic and the in-flight KV-prefetch circuit causes transient kernel mis-selection and aggressive cross-tenant prefetch eviction, increasing scheduling jitter and causing both TTFT and token-rate drops. Our initial mitigations (batching and global shedder) reduce pressure but do not fully prevent the micro-waves.

Mitigation plan (short-term / immediate):
- Implement a "slab-circuit-protector" routing guard that: 1) detects short-lived eviction waves on a slab, 2) temporarily reroutes new priming/short-context requests away from the slab for 15–45s, and 3) applies conservative kernel-selection lock to avoid mid-priming kernel flips.
- Deploy the guard as a dynamic feature-flag behind the runtime-ops toggles, roll out first to a small percentage (5%) of Hosted traffic and to a staging Dedicated cluster.
- For Private customers who escalate, provide a targeted toggle and assist with config changes.

Longer-term fixes:
- Rework KV-prefetch quarantine logic to prefer tenant-local LRU buckets and avoid global eviction storms.
- Add kernel-selection stability heuristics (minimum dwell time) when slab is under reconfiguration.
- Improve tracing to correlate slab eviction counters directly with TTFT regressions for automated alerts.

Verification and acceptance criteria:
- 95th-percentile TTFT returns to within 1.2x of baseline for windows similar to previous incidents in canary after 30m of steady traffic.
- Tokens/sec for representative replay workloads improves to within 90% of baseline.
- No increased error rates or tail CPU/GPU saturations introduced by the protector.

Rollout plan:
1) Feature-flagged deploy to runtime-ops staging (done).
2) Canary 5% Hosted traffic + 1 Dedicated staging cluster for 4 hours with expanded telemetry (scheduled).
3) If stable, ramp to 25% for 1 hour, then 100% across Hosted. Dedicated rollouts coordinated with account owners.
4) Private customers: provide config and one-off assistance; optional backport.

Communication:
- Customer bridge channel opened for the top 3 affected customers; daily status updates until stabilized.
- Incident postmortem doc (internal) to be created after final verification.

Notes: Because this interacts with both routing and KV subsystems, assume a conservative rollout and keep automatic rollback on failure.
